direct_answer: Aker BP integrates sustainability-related performance into its variable remuneration through the company bonus programme, which applies to all permanent employees, including management. Approximately 22% of the bonus potential is dependent on “sustainability-related initiatives and targets” [Source 1]. The bonus is calculated using a performance management system where delivery on company initiatives and KPIs feeds into the bonus; the scheme uses seven of eight equally weighted KPIs (plus initiative achievements and delivery on time/cost/quality for key field development projects) as the basis for variable remuneration [Source 4]. Sustainability-related KPIs explicitly included in the bonus framework include Safety (serious incidents), Equity share scope 1 GHG intensity, and “People and organisation” (based on employee feedback) [Source 4], and the company notes that three of eight KPIs directly address key sustainability aspects such as safety, GHG emission intensity and people/organisation [Source 5]. Governance-wise, the Organisational Development and Compensation Committee (ODCC) is responsible for ensuring remuneration arrangements support the company’s strategy, including sustainability matters [Source 2], and it oversees the setting of targets and monitoring of progress related to KPIs linked to the incentive schemes for executive management team (EMT) remuneration [Source 3].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide evidence that sustainability-related performance affects variable remuneration (22% of bonus potential) and identify sustainability-related KPIs used in the bonus framework, as well as ODCC oversight for EMT incentive-linked KPIs [Sources 1, 3, 4, 5]. However, the retrieved text does not specify the approval/update level for incentive scheme terms, does not describe key characteristics specifically for administrative/supervisory bodies (e.g., Board remuneration), and does not clearly distinguish which sustainability targets/impacts apply specifically to members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies versus the broader employee population [Sources 1, 3, 4].
disclosure_gaps: Whether sustainability-linked incentives/remuneration apply to members of the administrative and supervisory bodies (e.g., Board of Directors) specifically, and if so, the scheme design for those bodies (not just employees/management generally).

Clear identification of the specific sustainability-related targets/impacts used for remuneration assessment (beyond naming KPIs) and how they are measured/weighted within the sustainability-linked portion.

Explicit description of how sustainability performance metrics are embedded in remuneration policies/benchmarks for each relevant body (administrative, management, supervisory), including any long-term incentive plans if applicable.
Proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability-related targets/impacts for EMT/board separately (only an overall ~22% bonus potential figure is provided).
The level in the undertaking at which the terms of the incentive schemes are approved and updated (e.g., Board, committee, general meeting), as required by ESRS 2 GOV-3.
key_findings: Approximately 22% of bonus potential is dependent on sustainability-related initiatives and targets; the bonus is paid to all permanent employees, including management [Source 1].

Variable remuneration (bonus) is driven by delivery on initiatives and KPIs; seven of eight equally weighted KPIs are used as the basis (plus initiative achievements and project delivery on time/cost/quality) [Source 4].
Sustainability-related KPIs in the bonus framework include Safety and Equity share scope 1 GHG intensity; people & organisation is tracked via employee feedback [Source 4].

ODCC is tasked with ensuring remuneration supports strategy including sustainability matters, and oversees target-setting and progress monitoring for KPIs linked to EMT incentive schemes [Sources 2, 3].
